To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PD is a growing health problem with a substantial burden of disease and economic cost in the United States; (2) PD prevalence is likely to double by the year 2040; (3) the economic burden of PD will grow substantially over the coming decades as the size and age of the population with PD grows; (4) the economic burden is driven by medical costs and indirect costs (e.g., reduced employment) and is likely to grow at a similar rate to medical costs

1) PD prevalence in the U.S. will double by 2042; 2) PD-related healthcare costs are projected to increase by $4.2 billion between 2010 and 2040; and 3) PD-related nonmedical costs are projected to rise $2.3 billion between 2012 and 2040

(1) the number of people with PD will increase substantially in the coming decades; (2) the total economic burden of PD in the United States will also increase substantially in the future; and (3) the burden of PD is substantial, even in the current year.
